fields.meta_description: Build an insurance verification form patients fill in before the visit, with card photos and a staff section for what the plan confirms. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Insurance Verification Form Patients Finish Before the Visit
fields.hero_description: Build an insurance verification form that collects each patient's plan and card photos, then logs what the office confirms.
fields.features_heading: Two Sections, One Record per Patient
fields.features_subheading: An insurance verification form has two halves: what the patient tells you and what the plan confirms. Both save to one record.
fields.feature_1:
A patient section sent at booking

The patient enters the plan name, member ID, group number, and the phone number on the back of the card. The link goes out at booking, so answers arrive before check-in.
fields.feature_2:
Both sides of the card, photographed

Two upload fields take a photo of the front and back of the insurance card. Staff check the photo against the typed member ID instead of asking the patient at the desk.
fields.feature_3:
Policyholder fields only when needed

One question asks whether the patient is the policyholder. A no opens fields for that person's name, date of birth, employer, and relationship to the patient. A yes skips them all.
fields.feature_4:
A staff section for the benefits call

After calling the plan, staff record the copay, deductible left, visit limit, prior authorization status, and the call reference number. Patients never see this part of the form.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts before a gap reaches the visit

Pick the conditions that need a person, such as a scan with no authorization number or a plan near its visit limit. The app sends that record to the right person by email or Slack.
fields.feature_6:
Records in a database you own

Answers and staff notes save to a database you own, and the full code exports to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A returning patient's next check starts from this record.

fields.tab_content_1:
Card photos and plan details arrive before the cleaning

New patients at Bellmoor Family Dental get the form by email when they book. Delphine Arroyo filled hers in 3 days before her cleaning and attached photos of both sides of her card. Her record lands on the front desk's list marked ready to verify. Nobody retypes a member ID from a photocopy at check-in.
fields.tab_content_2:
Visits left drop to 3, and her therapist gets an email

Once the call to the plan ends, the Tillbrook Physical Therapy front desk fills in the staff section for Sunniva Holt. She has a $30 copay, $250 of deductible left, and 17 of 20 visits used this year. With 3 visits left, the app emails her therapist, Imani Brooke, before another session goes on the calendar.
fields.tab_content_3:
Answering no opens the parent's own section

Marisol Kowalczyk fills in the form for her 15-year-old son, a client at Marlow Bend Counseling who is covered on her plan. Her no to the policyholder question opens a new section, where she enters her name and employer. She then types her signature to confirm the details are correct.
fields.tab_content_4:
At 3 p.m., Slack gets every unverified scan

Tomorrow's schedule at Pell Street Imaging has 24 scans, and 21 are verified. At 3 p.m. the app posts the other 3 to the #scheduling Slack channel. One is an MRI marked as needing prior authorization, with no authorization number on file yet, and a scheduler picks it up before the end of the day.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an Insurance Verification Form
fields.howto_description: Follow 7 steps to build an insurance verification form that collects plan details early and records what the plan confirms.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Give the form a patient part and a staff part. Patients see only theirs, which keeps the link short enough to finish on a phone. Staff open the full record after calling the plan and add what it confirmed.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Label each field the way the card prints it, word for word. A patient holding the card can then match every box to a line on it. Mark each field required, because a call to the plan stalls on the first missing number.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add two upload fields, one for each side of the card, and require both for new patients. With a clear photo on file, staff can read a smudged member ID for themselves and correct a typo before they dial.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the policyholder question near the top. When the answer is no, ask for the policyholder's details and a typed signature from whoever fills in the form, such as a parent filling it in for a child.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write down what the front desk asks on every benefits call, in the order it asks, and give each answer its own field. End with the call reference number, the caller's initials, and the call date. Anyone reading the record later can see who checked and when.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide which records need a person before the visit, such as a missing authorization number or a plan close to its visit limit. Name the person or Slack channel for each one, and the time of day the check runs.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Fill in the patient link on your own phone, then complete the staff section as if the call to the plan had ended a minute ago. Check that both parts land in one record and that each alert reaches the person you named.

faq_plan.q: What is an insurance verification form?
faq_plan.a: An insurance verification form is the record a medical or dental office keeps of a patient's health plan. Insurance verification forms hold what the patient reports, such as the member ID and group number, and what staff confirm when they call the plan before the visit.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an insurance verification form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the form to Emergent's AI form builder: the patient fields, the staff call section, and who should hear about a gap. It builds the form, the database behind it, and the staff view from that prompt. Change any field later by asking for the change in plain English.

faq_plan.q: What should an insurance verification form template include?
faq_plan.a: Include the patient's name and date of birth, the plan name, the member and group numbers, and photos of both sides of the card. Add policyholder fields for when the patient is not the policyholder. Then give staff their own section for what the plan confirmed on the call, with the call reference number and date.

faq_plan.q: When should a practice send an insurance verification form to a new patient?
faq_plan.a: Send it as soon as the visit is booked. A patient who books a week out then has days, not minutes at the front desk, to find the card. A specialist who takes new patients through a referral form can send the insurance link the day the referral is accepted.

faq_plan.q: Should an insurance verification form ask whether a visit needs prior authorization?
faq_plan.a: Yes, in the staff section. HealthCare.gov's glossary says "Your health insurance or plan may require preauthorization for certain services before you receive them, except in an emergency." Give staff a yes or no field and a box for the authorization number. The same glossary adds that preauthorization isn't a promise the plan will cover the cost.

faq_plan.q: How should an insurance verification form handle a patient with two plans?
faq_plan.a: Ask for both. Add a question about a second plan, and when the answer is yes, open a second set of plan fields with its own card photos. Have staff confirm the order on the call. For patients with Medicare and other coverage, Medicare's guidance says "The insurance that pays first (primary payer) pays up to the limits of its coverage."

faq_plan.q: Should an insurance verification form ask for a photo ID as well as the card?
faq_plan.a: Only if your office checks identity at the same visit. A card photo shows the plan details, not who is holding the card. When you need both, collect the ID on a separate identity verification form and link the two records by patient. Emergent can build both forms on the same database.

faq_plan.q: Should an insurance verification form record the copay and the deductible?
faq_plan.a: Yes, both, dated the day of the call. Write down how much of the deductible is left on that date, next to the copay amount. HealthCare.gov's glossary defines a deductible as "The amount you pay for covered health care services before your insurance plan starts to pay."

faq_plan.q: Can patients fill out an insurance verification form on their phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The patient opens the emailed link in a phone browser, with no insurance verification form PDF to print or scan. Emergent can build it to show one question per screen, which suits someone reading numbers off a card held in the other hand. The answers save to the same record as the staff section.

faq_plan.q: Is there a free insurance verification form builder with no response limit?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing an insurance verification form. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps, whether 20 patients book this week or 2,000.

plan.angle: The top 10 is fillable PDFs from provider offices and agencies (a chiropractic insurer's sample, a dental office, an allergy college's sample, state motor-vehicle and benefits forms) plus one e-sign builder. Each is a blank sheet the front desk prints, hands over and types up. This page wins with the practice-side version: a patient section sent when the visit is booked (plan, member ID, group number, card photos, policyholder details only when the patient is not the policyholder) and an office section the staff fill in after calling the plan (copay, deductible left, visit limits, prior authorization, call reference). Then the app acts on it: a visit-limit alert to the treating therapist and a list of unverified scans posted to the scheduling channel the afternoon before.
